chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Khalid al-Asamm who said:

I performed Hajj with a group of our companions, and a woman was with us. When we arrived in Mecca, a man from our companions came and said, 'O you all, I have been tested.' We said, 'With what?' He said, 'I had sexual intercourse with this woman.' So ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). We asked him, and he said, 'Upon him is a camel.' The woman said, 'Ask for me Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), for I have also desired [sexual intercourse].' We asked him, and he said, 'Upon her is a camel.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'When he runs between al-Safa and al-Marwa, up to the saying
. Its explanation has already passed in the Chapter of Running (al-Sa'y).

Then he said: 'And whoever trims any of his nails, upon him is to feed a poor person one mudd of food for each nail. If he trims the nails of both his hands entirely, upon him is the blood of a sheep.'

key_terms.السَّعْي: The ritual running between the hills of Safa and Marwa.
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A specific type of sacrificial animal, typically a camel, used as expiation for major Ihram violations.
key_terms.شَكَرْتُ: I had sexual intercourse (literally: I gave thanks).
key_terms.مُدّ: A traditional unit of volume for measuring food.

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for trimming nails while in Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific expiations (kaffarah) for minor violations of Ihram conditions, highlighting the distinction between major acts like sexual intercourse, which require a camel (badanah), and minor acts like trimming nails, which require feeding the poor. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on proportional compensation based on the severity of the transgression, linking physical grooming to charitable obligations. The text also references the broader context of Ihram restrictions, such as walking between Safa and Marwa, to situate these rulings within the complete ritual framework.
